description:
## Proven problem

Parallel fixture matrices on the fz-tfn.26 base and the fz-tfn.27 implementation reproduced fixture_command_rejects_missing_readiness failing because a no-ready child raced between pipe-EOF wording and child-exit wording. Isolated reruns passed unchanged. Two branches of the harness lifecycle owned different diagnostics for the same missing execution boundary.

## Goal and ownership

Classify missing readiness once, independently of whether EOF or child exit is observable first. FixtureCommandState combines the required boundary, accumulated readiness bytes, pipe openness, and observed process status. Zero bytes plus either EOF or exit yields MissingExecutionReady. One formatter reports the label, missing boundary, zero readiness bytes, and captured stderr after group teardown and leader reaping. Exit status is deliberately excluded from this harness error because EOF may require killing a still-live leader. Successful signaled commands retain their real exit status and captured output.

Observe process status before draining readiness so an exited child's final buffered signal is consumed before classification. Keep setup/execution timeout policy and compiler behavior unchanged. Reuse existing group teardown and anonymous-file output ownership.

## TDD evidence

Before the classification change, two deterministic subprocess probes failed in one cargo invocation (handle80964, terminal101, 0 passed / 2 failed): an EOF-first child blocked on its stdin control pipe produced the old pipe-only diagnostic; the same child released and explicitly reaped before readiness observation produced the old exit-status diagnostic. Both expected one exact diagnostic including setup stderr. Ordering uses pipe readiness and child wait, with no scheduling sleeps or retries.

After the change, all three focused readiness trials pass (handle79152, terminal0). The ordered probes assert the same structured MissingExecutionReady verdict and exact diagnostic, then prove the direct child is reaped. The third trial verifies buffered readiness after an already-observed exit, successful and nonzero exit status preservation, and exact stderr for a nonzero no-ready child. Existing tests cover inherited background readiness writers, anonymous capture writers, setup guards, outer test-command signals, and delegated-root timeout cleanup.

## Acceptance and remaining gates

Run repeated complete parallel fixture matrices, formatting and strict clippy; record terminal outcomes before closure. Fresh root cold review, isolated ticket commit and closure remain with the root agent. No timeout increase, alternate-string assertion, compiler change, or new temporary fixture remains. Harness documentation is updated in .agent/docs/fixtures.md.
title: Make readiness EOF failure classification deterministic under parallel fixture load
